newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Report key Argentine murder suspect may give up.
newsitem.headline: Report key Argentine murder suspect may give up.

text.p: A suspect in the murder of an Argentine news photographer has offered to name the person who pulled the trigger in return for a reduced prison term, the newspaper Clarin said on Saturday.

"One of the suspects still at large in the murder of Jose Luis Cabezas has agreed to turn himself in to the police and give the name of the person who shot the photographer, in return for the reduced sentences offered by (Buenos Aires province) Gov. Eduardo Duhalde," Clarin said.
Gov. Duhalde, a presidential hopeful, said Friday he was willing to extend an offer for lenient punishment to informers who were actually involved in the crime.
The suspect, Jose Luis Auge, a handyman whose brother is a policeman, is believed to have been among those who took Cabezas to the place where he was killed in January, Clarin said.

The charred body of 35-year-old Cabezas, who worked for the news magazine Noticias, was found in a car near the Atlantic resort of Pinamar. He was handcuffed, beaten, shot in the head, doused with fuel and burned to a blackened skeleton.
The murder horrified Argentina, reviving dark memories of the "death squads" of the 1970s, and has led to widespread outcry and street protests.
Gov. Duhalde said Friday another suspect arrested this week had identified an ex-policeman suspected of the murder.
The informer was among four people, including two police officers, arrested on Wednesday on the orders of Judge Jose Luis Macchi. Another ex-policeman was arrested on Friday.

In his eight-hour confession Thursday, the informer, Miguel Retana, told Macchi how the ex-policeman paid him and four others to "scare" Cabezas. He said the plan later went horribly wrong when Cabezas recognised one of the assailants.
The media identified the man who hired Retana as Gustavo Prellezo, a former inspector for the Buenos Aires Province Police and one of the four suspects arrested Wednesday.
Prellezo's wife, policewoman Silvia Belausky who was also arrested, was released Saturday on lack of evidence.

Retana said he was hired "to beat up a photographer" who was investigating a crime wave on the coast run by corrupt officers of the Buenos Aires force, which has a terrible reputation for corruption and brutality.
